verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; STOP raised and repaired for three GCM TLS-IV length arms that reproduced an authority out-of-bounds write through wrapping size_t arithmetic, and for the in-place DES3-WRAP unwrap whose shift used the reversed ptr::copy argument order and formed an out-of-block pointer. No unrepaired memory-safety defect, ABI regression, hidden obligation or remaining unsafe-safe-Rust API.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the shared provider decoder front doors (PEM-to-DER, EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo-to-PrivateKeyInfo, SubjectPublicKeyInfo-to-type-specific and DER-to-key), the shared provider context, the AES/ARIA/SM4 GCM engine and its three hardware rows, the DES3-WRAP cipher engine, and the DSA WITH MD DER writer. evp/method_store.rs was deferred again as the method-store registry boundary; provider/der_dsa_sig.rs was substituted from position 9 of the queue. Data classes: GCM/TDES IVs, tags, AAD, OIDs, algorithm names, dispatch tables and SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER are PUBLIC_DATA; passphrases, decrypted PrivateKeyInfo bytes and private-key DER are SECRET_DATA. No constant-time claim is made for any file from source inspection.

defects.class: authority undefined behaviour reproduced (wrapping size_t subtraction -> out-of-bounds store)
defects.description: getivgen increments the invocation field at ctx->iv + ctx->ivlen - 8. The whole-IV restore arm of gcm_tls_iv_set_fixed sets iv_gen without requiring ivlen >= 8, so an application can reach getivgen with ivlen 1..7. The C authority computes an in-struct pointer and corrupts the preceding members; the Rust transcription's wrapping_sub formed a wildly out-of-bounds pointer and ctr64_inc wrote through it. Reachable from the public OSSL_CIPHER_PARAM_AEAD_TLS1_GET_IV_GEN parameter path.
defects.fix: Refuse with 0 when ivlen < 8, before hw->setiv and the increment. Legitimate TLS GCM IVs are 12 bytes, so no valid call changes. The # Safety contract still states the callee obligations; the guard is the caller-side elimination of the authority's mechanism (§17).
defects.witness: ciphercommon_gcm.c:116-132; ciphercommon_gcm.c:790-813 (restore arm sets iv_gen with no length check); new test provider::cipher_gcm::tests::the_tls_iv_length_arms_refuse_wrapped_lengths.

defects.class: authority undefined behaviour reproduced (unvalidated data_size -> underflowed memcpy offset)
defects.description: setivinv copies inl bytes to ctx->iv + ctx->ivlen - inl. Its documented precondition inl <= ivlen was not established by ossl_gcm_set_ctx_params, which forwards the application-supplied OSSL_PARAM data_size unchanged. In the authority an inl above ivlen wraps the subtraction and writes outside ctx->iv; in Rust the same wrapping_sub produced an out-of-bounds write. Reachable from OSSL_CIPHER_PARAM_AEAD_TLS1_SET_IV_INV.
defects.fix: Refuse with 0 when inl > ctx->ivlen, before the copy. The valid explicit-IV call uses 8 bytes against a 12-byte IV, so behaviour is unchanged on every legitimate path.
defects.witness: ciphercommon_gcm.c:134-146; ciphercommon_gcm.c:606-612 (caller passes p.inviv->data_size); new test provider::cipher_gcm::tests::the_tls_iv_length_arms_refuse_wrapped_lengths.

defects.class: authority undefined behaviour reproduced (wrapped guard admits memcpy/RAND_bytes_ex with an underflowed length)
defects.description: gcm_tls_iv_set_fixed guards with (ivlen - len) < 8 in size_t. For len > ivlen the subtraction wraps, the guard passes, and the authority copies len bytes and draws ivlen - len into ctx->iv + len. With GCM_IV_MAX_SIZE 128 a len above ivlen is still inside the iv array for the copy but the RAND length wraps. The Rust transcription reproduced the wrap with wrapping_sub and would pass a near-SIZE_MAX length to RAND_bytes_ex. Reachable from OSSL_CIPHER_PARAM_AEAD_TLS1_IV_FIXED.
defects.fix: Added len > ctx->ivlen to the guard, so the subtraction below is only evaluated when no wrap is possible. A valid fixed-IV call has len <= ivlen - 8.

defects.class: conversion defect (source/destination reversed) -> wrong plaintext on every in-place unwrap
defects.description: The in-place shift was written ptr::copy(out, out.add(8), inl - 8), but Rust's ptr::copy takes the source first. The authority's memmove(out, out + 8, inl - 8) (cipher_tdes_wrap.c:57) shifts the central blocks left; the transcription shifted them right, so the central decrypt read the first eight bytes twice and the final IV read the wrong block. Any EVP_DecryptUpdate performed in place (the normal record path) produced a wrong result or a spurious ICV failure against OpenSSL.
defects.fix: ptr::copy(out.add(8), out, inl - 8), the authority's direction. The new read-sequence test records every block the hardware callback is handed and requires the in-place and out-of-place forms to read the same byte sequence; it fails on the pre-repair direction and passes on the repair.

defects.class: out-of-block pointer arithmetic (Rust UB) used to express the shifted read offsets
defects.description: The transcription reproduced the authority's in -= 8, which forms a pointer eight bytes before the caller's block. The authority never dereferences it (the +8 and +inl-8 below add it back), but Rust pointer arithmetic requires every intermediate offset to stay in bounds of the allocation.
defects.fix: The two reads it denotes are now computed directly: an in-place central read starts at the original in, and the shifted final block is at in + inl - 16. The in-place read-sequence test witnesses the equivalence.

defects.class: secret residue on a stack buffer and on plain heap releases (deliberate improvement over the authority)
defects.description: The OSSL_PASSPHRASE_CALLBACK copy in pbuf[1024] is SECRET_DATA and was left on the stack; the decrypted PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO bytes in new_der and the input DER block (which can itself be a plaintext PrivateKeyInfo) were released with plain CRYPTO_free. The authority does the same at decode_epki2pki.c:172-205, :232 and :152.
defects.fix: OPENSSL_cleanse(pbuf, 1024) on both the refusal and success arms; cleanse new_der over its plaintext length before its OwnedBlock release; cleanse the decode block over der_len before its release. Release sites and allocator-seam coordinates are unchanged, and no observable behaviour changes.
defects.witness: decode_epki2pki.c:159-234; tests provider::decode_epki2pki (dispatch shape and zero-state sweep) remain green.

defects.class: secret residue on a plain heap release (deliberate improvement over the authority)
defects.description: PEM_do_header decrypts a private key in place in the der block, and a bare PRIVATE KEY/EC PRIVATE KEY PEM is already plaintext key DER. The authority releases the block with a plain OPENSSL_free (decode_pem2der.c:321).
defects.fix: After the label block, cleanse der over der_len before the existing OwnedBlock release. The success and the decryption-failure paths are both covered (on failure der_len is the still-allocated ciphertext length).
defects.witness: decode_pem2der.c:283-325; tests provider::decode_pem2der (dispatch shape and zero-state sweep) remain green.

defects.class: secret residue on a plain heap release (deliberate improvement over the authority)
defects.description: The block ossl_read_der returns carries the input DER, which is private-key material on every private-key row. The authority releases it with a plain OPENSSL_free on both the fatal and the next: tails (decode_der2key.c:395, :419).
defects.fix: A new unsafe helper cleanse_der(der, der_len) wipes the block before the single OwnedBuf release on both tails. The helper's contract states provenance, ownership and that der_len never exceeds the allocation; it is called only from the owning frame.
defects.witness: decode_der2key.c:246-419; tests provider::decode_der2key (tables, selection rule and zero-state sweep) remain green.

residuals: src/evp/method_store.rs remains the deferred method-store registry boundary.

The decoded key objects released by the row free functions (DH_free, DSA_free, EC_KEY_free, RSA_free, the ML/SLH key frees) and by the PKCS8 item destructor are not cleansed; that is the authority's item-destructor contract and is preserved, not reclassified as safe.

GCM/TDES keys are expanded into the context's own schedule; the original key buffer is caller-owned and is not copied or released by these units. The context block is released with CRYPTO_clear_free, which wipes the schedule.

The GCM guards refuse inputs the authority turns into memory corruption; this is a deliberate safety divergence (§17), not a compatibility claim. A court that probes overlength tlsivfixed/tlsivinv data will see the refusal rather than the authority's corruption.
decode_spki2typespki's DER is SubjectPublicKeyInfo (PUBLIC_DATA) and keeps the authority's plain release; the epki/der2key/pem2der DER blocks are cleansed because they can carry private-key material.
No constant-time claim is made for any GCM, TDES or decoder unit from source inspection.
